title: Losing Leverage: A Game-Theoretic Simulation of Power After Full Automation
description: Throughout history, rulers have needed large numbers of people to work, to pay taxes, and to enforce orders. That need is what made them bargain with, feed and fear their populations, despite the class contempt on both sides. If intellectual and physical automation can handle all productive and military work, the need dissolves. This paper asks what protects people once it does, using a game-theoretic Monte Carlo simulation of seventeen world actors from 2026 to 2075. It tracks: AI capability and robot build-out; the loss of the public's economic and military leverage; the erosion of democracy; purges inside ruling groups; and the choices those groups make once their populations are no longer needed. It draws on evidence from history, political science, economics and AI forecasting, and includes four restraints on rulers that survived adversarial review against documented cases. We cross-checked it against a pre-specified elicitation from a judgment model. Like war games and the scenario side of climate research, the model cannot predict when events will happen. It can, however, compare futures and show which assumptions drive them. Under its stated assumptions, events unfold in this order. Democracy erodes first: in the US it breaks down in 83% of runs by 2050, and in a fifth of all runs already by 2030. People stop being needed in the leading bloc by a median year of 2034. Rights go within a few years: the US or China public loses its rights in about 80% of runs, 68% of runs by 2040. Killing follows by escalation, mostly from the 2040s: a deliberate loss of 10% or more of the US or China population reaches 50% by 2075, and a loss of 99.9% or more reaches 42%. An income network outside state and corporate control, carrying 50% of US-bloc economic activity by the early 2030s, halves the near-total risk to 2050. These numbers show where the assumptions lead, not a forecast. Code, data and results: https://github.com/autonet-code/leverage-sims
